title: Does anybody know what trustable website i can go to find and purchase 35/16mm film reels

commenti.body: I don't know where you can find reels, but if you are interested in film restoration, the place to start would be your local film archive. Small film archives are often looking for help and they do vital archiving and restoration work that they can train you to do. They also already have film scanning machines and all the equipment already, along with fridges and freezers that are designed to store film reels. I know you're looking to do something specific, but preserving your local history on film is important work, and it can give you the tools you need to work on the marx brothers films.
The grand local film archive of my hometown. RIGHT! I don't think there is one.

You might be surprised! If there's a university or a heritage center around, there could be. But for people to talk to about your restoration plans, you could start here https://www.fiafnet.org/ it's the international film archive federation, there's contact information for many archives, and articles and information that may be useful for what you want to do. Somebody there will know how to help you I'm sure!
Take a guess how old I am and where I live.

Back in the 90s, I was interested in film preservation and, on a whim, reached out to Robert A. Harris (restored Lawrence of Arabia, among many other films). He responded and asked where I was located. It turned out that the Library of Congress had their nitrate film vaults in Dayton, OH at the time, which was about an hour’s drive from me. He put me in touch with the Vault Leader there, who set me up with a volunteer gig at their facility. Best year of my life spent there learning about film and film history and getting my hands dirty in the vaults. Long story short, you never know what opportunities are waiting nearby, even if you aren’t exactly in a major city.
Does it still exist, because ironically I live in Ohio.

Unfortunately, no. They moved to a fantastic new facility in Culpepper, VA some years back. It's a good thing, because the facility they had been using was literally a WWII-era vault facility at Wright Patterson AFB. It was grody.

The Ohio History Connection has an audiovisual archive, it's not exactly what you're looking for, but it could be interesting nonetheless [https://www.ohiohistory.org/research/archives-library/manuscripts-audiovisual-collections/](https://www.ohiohistory.org/research/archives-library/manuscripts-audiovisual-collections/)
